title: Slow-cooker creamy garlic chicken
subtitle: Chicken breasts in a rich, garlicky cream cheese sauce
excerpt: Chicken breasts slow-cooked in stock and cream cheese with plenty of garlic. The sauce is thick, rich, and very good over rice or pasta.
sourceNotes: Creamy garlic chicken is a popular slow-cooker recipe in British and American home cooking, adapted from stovetop chicken in cream sauce. No single canonical source; common in slow-cooker cookbooks from the 2010s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made a day ahead and kept in the fridge. Reheat gently on the hob and serve with freshly cooked chicken.

content.text: Cream cheese is the key ingredient here. It melts into the chicken stock during cooking and forms a thick, rich sauce without any need for a separate roux or reduction. The result is a dish that tastes like it took much longer than it did.

Chicken breasts work well here because the low, moist heat keeps them from drying out. Keep the cook time to 3 to 4 hours on LOW; much longer and the texture will start to degrade. If you want to cook for longer, use chicken thighs instead.
Serve over pasta, rice, or mashed potato. Steamed broccoli or green beans work well alongside.

Add {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock to the slow cooker. Drop in {{cream-cheese}} of cream cheese in spoonfuls. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, {{italian-seasoning}} of Italian seasoning, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt, and {{black-pepper-ground}} of black pepper. Stir until the cream cheese begins to incorporate.
Place {{chicken-breast}} chicken breasts in the sauce. Spoon some of the sauce over the top of each breast.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 3 to 4 hours. Do not exceed 4 hours or the chicken breasts will begin to dry out. The sauce will be thick and creamy when done. Shred the chicken with two forks or serve whole. Scatter with chopped parsley if using.

rows.symptom: The sauce has split and looks grainy
rows.cause: Cream cheese can split if the temperature is too high or if low-fat cream cheese was used.
rows.fix: Stir vigorously to bring it back together. A splash of hot water or stock can help. Next time use full-fat cream cheese only, and stick to LOW.

rows.cause: Chicken breast overcooks easily in a slow cooker. Even 30 minutes past 4 hours on LOW can dry it out.
rows.fix: Next time use chicken thighs, which tolerate longer cooking. Shred the meat and stir it through the sauce to help it absorb moisture.

rows.cause: The chicken released liquid during cooking, diluting the sauce.
rows.fix: Mix a teaspoon of cornflour with a tablespoon of cold water and stir it into the sauce. Set to HIGH with the lid off for 15 minutes to thicken.

rows.symptom: The garlic taste is too strong
rows.cause: Raw garlic cooked slowly intensifies in a closed pot.
rows.fix: Next time use 3 cloves instead of 6, or use roasted garlic for a milder, sweeter result.

content.text: Creamy garlic chicken became a slow-cooker staple in British and American homes during the 2010s. It is one of the most-searched slow-cooker recipes online. The appeal is straightforward: very few ingredients, a short prep time, and a result that feels more effort than it was.
